Maya (Support): FYI customer `acme-health` opened a P1 — traffic for EU tenant got routed to us-west and they received a RESIDENCY_VIOLATION. High latency, plus audit alert fired. Repro details below. :warning:

Maya (Support): curl + response snippet:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?model=redwood-2-eu"
# response (from us-west-2):
{"error":{"code":"RESIDENCY_VIOLATION","msg":"request served from us-west-2 for tenant acme-health-eu"}}
```

Ravi (SRE): @Maya thanks — can you paste the request_id and the exact timestamp? Also did they see a fallback header (X-Redwood-Fallback: true)? :eyes:

Maya (Support): Request-id `r-abc123-x9`, client timestamp `2026-02-28T14:12:43Z`. They reported `X-Redwood-Fallback: eu->us-west2` in response headers and round-trip ~2200ms.

ops-bot: AuditLog created -> id: `audit-5882`, rule: `residency.enforced`, tenant: `acme-health-eu`, event_ts: `2026-02-28T14:12:44Z`.

Tom (Eng - Runtime): Initial hypothesis: routing policy did an automated fallback because eu-central pool reported degraded capacity. Two things to check: 1) routing decision trace (`rtrctl trace <request_id>`), 2) autoscaler health events around the time window.

Ravi (SRE): Running trace now:
```
$ rtrctl trace r-abc123-x9 --format=lines
route: tenant=acme-health-eu -> candidate=eu-central(priority=100)
healthcheck: eu-central -> transient_unhealthy (timeout 10s)
fallback: selected us-west-2 (priority=70, compatible_variant=redwood-2-small)
served_from: us-west-2 (node nid-07a3)
headers: X-Redwood-Fallback=true
```

Elena (Compliance): This triggered a policy exception in our Data Residency scanner. We need a full audit export for the customer and an incident notification pack. Marking as compliance P1 — customer contracts require EU-only.

Maya (Support): I've informed the customer that we're investigating and temporarily disabling automatic fallback for their tenant while we triage. They accepted follow-up.

Ravi (SRE): Mitigation steps applied: pinned `acme-health-eu` to `eu-central` variant and set `fallback=none` via admin console for that tenant. Commands run:
```
adminctl tenant update acme-health-eu --route=eu-central --fallback=none --note="temp lock after residency alert"
```
Result: subsequent request `r-abc124` served from eu-central, no residency alert and latency ~180ms.

deploy-bot: policy-change event -> change_id `chg-9921`, user `ravi`, status -> applied.

Tom (Eng - Runtime): Root cause analysis (quick): the eu-central healthcheck was intermittently timing out due to a bad probe change (health probe used a deprecated /healthz header that returned 504 under certain load). I have a patch open: PR #4321 that reverts the probe and adds retries. Rolling a hotfix to routing healthcheck service now.

Tom (Eng - Runtime): Longer-term action items:
- Add tenancy-level residency guard to prevent automatic cross-region fallback for tenants with residency requirements.
- Add more granular healthcheck metrics (p95 latency + probe success ratio) to avoid false unhealthy flips.
- Audit 30d of fallback events and surface any other EU tenants that saw cross-region serving.

Elena (Compliance): Please add the audit export (s3 link) and redact any tokens before sharing with the customer. Compliance will draft the notification and coordinate legal review.

Maya (Support): Uploaded artifacts -> https://s3.redwood.com/incidents/1782345678/audit-export.csv (redacted). Notifying customer with timeline and mitigation steps.

Ravi (SRE): Post-mitigation monitoring: no further residency alerts for `acme-health-eu` in last 45m, autoscaler health check updated, hotfix deployed. Closing immediate incident but keeping postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:

Tom (Eng - Runtime): Assigning postmortem owner: @Tom. ETA for full RCA doc: 2026-03-03.

Elena (Compliance): Thanks team — keeping incident flagged for 30d retention and notifying contracts.

Maya (Support): Filing follow-up ticket for Billing to check if the cross-region requests generated any unexpected egress/billing events for the customer.

Ravi (SRE): Adding follow-up tasks to the incident board: RT-2240 (prevent residency fallback), RT-2241 (healthcheck metrics), RT-2242 (audit fallback history).

Maya (Support): Closing thread here — will add the postmortem link when ready. :lock:
